definition: Supports/advances a policy position, program, or normative goal.
notes: Primary pragmatic function; mutually exclusive. See codebook-v1.1.0 §5.1 / §4.3.1. If truly tied, choose function directed at primary political target; flag borderline=true (≤5% expected).

definition: Challenges an actor's competence, integrity, legitimacy, or record.
notes: Primary pragmatic function; mutually exclusive. Independent of fallacy labels. See §5.2 / §4.3.1–§4.3.2 / §4.3.4.

definition: Rebuts criticism or protects actor/policy reputation when prior criticism is recoverable from the unit or allowed ±1 context.
notes: Primary pragmatic function; mutually exclusive. See §5.3 / §4.3.4 / context policy §2.1.

definition: Commits to future action, concrete measure, or implementation pledge by this actor.
notes: Primary pragmatic function; mutually exclusive. See §5.4 / §4.3.3. Chair chamber voting announcements are PF_PROCEDURAL, not PF_PROPOSAL.

definition: Seeks electoral/civic support via identity, values, fear, hope, or solidarity.
notes: Primary pragmatic function; mutually exclusive. See §5.5 / §4.3.2.

definition: Conveys subject-matter factual information (policy, bill content, figures, technical description) with minimal evaluative framing. Not for chamber-management or vote-tally reporting.
notes: Primary pragmatic function; mutually exclusive. See codebook-v1.1.0 §5.6 / §4.2. Do not treat “procedural information” as PF_INFO.

definition: Avoids question/topic; pivots without substantive engagement.
notes: Primary pragmatic function; mutually exclusive. Rare in prepared plenary speech. See §5.7 / §4.3.5.

definition: Chamber management of the sitting (order of business, turn-taking, votes, timekeeping, suspension/resumption, agenda transitions), including factual statements about the proceeding itself. Function of utterance, not speaker identity.
notes: Primary pragmatic function; mutually exclusive. See codebook-v1.1.0 §5.8 / §4.2.
